content: Hello, one glance on your screen shot: it's a real mess you created by relocating message storage to another drive, and it would be very tricky to retrieve a working profile without many screen shots or having a look on your screen. Then copy & paste the backup of your folder Thunderbird in C:\Users\%username%\AppData\Roaming\ here. On restart Thunderbird should display all your old POP accounts, folders and messages. content:
Personally I would run a disk scan to validate the logical integrity of the hard disk. Nothing appear to bring windows to it's knees faster that hard disk failure or corruption.

Open File Explorer and click This PC. Right-click the drive you want to check (like C:) and select Properties. Go to the Tools tab. Click the Check button under Error checking. Select Scan drive. If the drive is in use, Windows will ask to schedule the check for your next restart and the c: drive almost always requires a restart as that is where windows is installed by default
